my_first_view: GtoPdb ligand 6852 (cache/gtopdb/interactions.csv, 9 human rows): pKi HDAC1 8.89, HDAC2 8.80, HDAC6 8.80, HDAC3 8.30, HDAC11 7.44, HDAC10 7.30, HDAC9 7.19, HDAC8 6.3-6.7, HDAC5 5.44 (about 3.6 uM). HDAC5 is class IIa, about 3 orders of magnitude weaker than class I/IIb; class IIa has a poorly reactive catalytic site so the low potency is expected, not noise. The proposal's main_target HDAC5 is therefore not the pharmacologically relevant target of vorinostat; the DGIdb twin lists all 11 HDACs with sign -1 and HDAC5 is just one of them, while the CHEMBL98 family has only HDAC1/2/3/6 (ChEMBL). Free hydroxamic acid is the active form (no prodrug, prodrug=0). The HDAC5 chain is unsound as a potency statement; at best a high-concentration off-target that can only be read as sign-of-class. Sign of HDAC5 -> SLC2A1 (+) from CollecTRI is a curated TF-edge for a non-DNA-binding co-regulator and its sign provenance needs checking.

topic: Pan-HDAC/HDAC6 arm for Q230P protein stability
my_first_view: Supportable only as conditional. Vorinostat does engage HDAC6 at 1.6 nM (pKi 8.8), so it is a real HDAC6 lever, unlike butyrate (card A01: butyrate does not engage HDAC6, the open item is exactly 'no pan-HDAC or HDAC6-selective arm exists'). But the same compound is a stronger class I inhibitor, and the card says a class-I inhibitor did not reproduce the soluble mutant gain and worsened an EEG count; the card defers the whole class until the lesion's fate and a wild-type function ruler exist. So an arm can be named as a conditional comparator (pan-HDAC, plus HDAC6-selective to separate), not as a candidate; CNS exposure of vorinostat unknown in the card.

topic: Reasons to investigate and shared origins
my_first_view: Reasons: (1) HDAC6/HSP90 acetylation, proteostasis arm of A01 (independent origin: card/literature); (2) class-I HDAC transcription of cDNA constructs (same pharmacology, different mechanism); (3) HDAC5 -> SLC2A1 expression chain (CollecTRI/TRRUST/ExTRI2 versions are one origin counted once); (4) reversal of the hNPC and organoid signatures (GSE126075 and GSE156243 share one IT7 derivation: one origin); (5) approval/accessibility status (not a reason of efficacy). Reasons 3 and 4 share the single expression-derivation origin; reason 1 is independent of them and is the only one tied to the Q230P question.
